title: Audit and simulator for partial-chunk crediting bias
creator: Ava Martinez
description: There are recurring discrepancies between client-visible token tallies and server-side ledger debits for long-lived streaming sessions that deliver partial chunks. Root causes appear to be a combination of tokenizer drift (client vs server pre-tokenization heuristics), midstream model handoffs, and out-of-order finalization semantics in the metering pipeline. This ticket builds a repeatable audit harness + traffic simulator to reproduce, measure, and propose fixes for partial-chunk crediting bias so we can quantify leakage and tighten guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay recorded production fragment traces and generate deterministic inputs for the meterer (both WS frames and HTTP-streamed chunks)
A set of end-to-end tests that reproduce the historical 0.5–2.3% divergence cases locally (within CI) and on a small staging cluster
A reconciliation tool that takes simulator output and server ledger rows and emits a per-session delta report (token_count_client, token_count_server, explanation_tags)
Two concrete mitigation proposals (one opt-in rollback/patch for hosted, one permanent fix) documented and prototyped
Metric dashboards (replay-success, delta-distribution, idempotency-failures) are created in Datadog and validate reduced divergence when mitigation is enabled
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Narrowed scope to streaming partial-chunk cases only (exclude batch synchronous endpoints) — decision by Ravi, Ava, and PM.
2026-02-20: Use 'shadow-metering' approach for initial experiments: run simulator against a parallel path that does not affect billing and compare outputs — agreed in tech review.

2026-03-04: Prioritize deterministic tokenization alignment over aggressive retroactive credits for initial rollout; plan is to fix tokenizer heuristics and introduce small retroactive reconciler later if needed.
2026-03-10: Rollout plan split: stage test with simulator-driven canary, then enable in 2 dedicated regions before full global rollout.
implementation_notes: Build a lightweight 'stream-replayer' (Go) that consumes sanitized production trace exports and can output: WebSocket frames, HTTP chunked responses, and interleaved control messages with configurable timing jitter.

Implement an 'audit logger' attachment to the metering pipeline that emits pre- and post-tokenization snapshots and a stable fragment-id for each partial chunk (hash of session_id + frame_offset + timestamp truncated).

Add deterministic tokenization mode flag to the tokenizer used by the meterer: when enabled, it uses the same normalization pipeline as client SDK (unicode normalization, attachment stripping, deterministic whitespace collapse).

Create a reconciliation job that ingests simulator input and ledger rows, computes per-fragment attribution, and surfaces mismatch categories: tokenizer-drift, duplication-dedup, late-finalize, model-handoff-variant.

Design a safe 'provisional rollback' flow (server-only) where if a replay shows a clear overcharge class and the session is within 72 hours, we surface a provisional credit candidate to finance ops for review.

notes_for_reviewers: Pay attention to the stable fragment-id design: hashing session_id + frame_offset + truncated_timestamp must be collision resistant across multi-tenant traffic but also deterministic across replay jitter.
The deterministic tokenizer is intentionally conservative — we prefer undercounting edge whitespace vs producing divergent token splits; want feedback from SDK owners on normalization parity.
